Meanwhile modern applications lean heavily on databases, and every slow query hurts users. A cache stores frequently requested data in fast memory; this simple idea can cut latency dramatically. Teams often place a cache between the application and the database.

However well designed, consistency remains the hardest part. When a record changes in the database, stale copies must be invalidated or refreshed; otherwise users may see outdated values. Common strategies include write-through, write-behind, and time-based expiration. Choosing the right cache policy depends on workload patterns, tolerance for staleness, and how expensive a cache miss becomes.

Along this path, monitoring is vital. Admins track hit ratios daily; a low ratio signals lost RAM and poor tuning. Good dashboards, strict limits, and solid warm-up plans all assist a busy app during traffic bursts, so it stays quick and handy for millions of visitors.

Finally teams must measure performance before and after adding a cache, since only real numbers prove the work is done.
